title: Nova Systems - POC scoping: workload modeling
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling: QPS, concurrency, input/output token distribution, latency SLOs. Agreement to run two benchmark profiles (interactive chat and batch summarization), share sample payloads, and target a 4-week POC with success criteria defined by latency p95 < 300ms for chat and cost within target ranges. Next steps: Redwood to send POC proposal, benchmark harness, and security docs; Nova to provide sample traffic and schedule benchmark window.
next_steps: Redwood to send POC proposal and pricing (Aisha) by 2026-03-17
Nova to share sample payloads and request traces (Priya) by 2026-03-19
Schedule benchmark run with Nova and Redwood SEs for week of 2026-03-23
Redwood to provide benchmark harness repo link and run instructions (Marco) by 2026-03-18
Follow-up sync after benchmark with results and recommended config (2-3 days after run)
action_items: Aisha Patel: Send formal POC proposal + pricing - due 2026-03-17
Marco Ruiz: Share benchmark harness (scripts + k6 config + README) - due 2026-03-18
Priya Nair: Provide sample payloads and 7-day traffic traces (anonymized) - due 2026-03-19
Sam Ortega: Confirm test window and provide egress/IP allowlist - due 2026-03-20
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to focus today on scoping the POC workload modeling for Nova Systems, make sure success criteria and benchmarks are clear.
[00:08] Evan Chen: Yeah thanks Aisha, appreciate it. We're looking to validate both interactive chat flows and nightly batch summarization jobs. Main concerns are latency for live chat and cost for batch.
[00:20] Marco Ruiz: Great, can you give us some numbers around QPS and concurrency for both profiles? Even ballpark helps shape instance selection and batching.
[00:30] Priya Nair: For chat, average QPS is around 8 during peak, with spikes to about 40 for short bursts. Concurrency-wise we typically see 10 to 20 concurrent chat sessions, but our front-end does some multiplexing so perceived concurrency can be higher.
[00:45] Aisha Patel: Got it. So peak QPS 40, steady 8. Any idea on tokens in/out for chat? Average prompt size?
[00:53] Priya Nair: Chat inputs average 60 tokens, outputs about 140 tokens. But we have a small percentage of long context sessions --- maybe 5% exceed 800 tokens in history.
[01:05] Marco Ruiz: That's valuable. For the POC we usually model a 95th percentile payload and an average payload. We'll set benchmark profiles: interactive chat (avg 60 / 140 tokens, p95 800 tokens) and extended context test.
[01:18] Sam Ortega: For batch summarization: nightly job runs roughly 2,500 documents, that's about 50K total input tokens and it runs on a 4-hour window. We care more about total throughput and cost than tail latency there.
[01:31] Kai Thompson: Quick question, are those documents parallelizable? i.e., are they independent pieces we can batch across multiple GPU slots?
[01:36] Priya Nair: Yes, they are independent — can be processed in parallel. We can chunk to 2k tokens per document on average.
[01:43] Aisha Patel: Perfect. For the interactive profile, what's your latency SLO? p95 or p99?
[01:48] Evan Chen: We want p95 under 300ms ideally, p99 under 600ms would be great, but we can be flexible during the POC as long as we see clear path to improvement.
[01:58] Marco Ruiz: That's ambitious but achievable with right model variant and batch sizing. Two levers we'll test: lower-latency model or smaller context with prefix caching, and routing to dedicated instances for steady traffic.
[02:10] Priya Nair: Cost targets? We have a monthly budget projection, but for the POC a hard requirement is that estimated per-1M-token cost for batch shouldn't exceed $150. For chat we want to project cost per active user per month.
[02:22] Aisha Patel: We'll produce cost estimates based on Redwood's Optimize recommendations: batching, quantization and KV cache. For batch workload we'll run both fp16 and int8 quant profiles to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[02:35] Marco Ruiz: On the benchmarks, we'll run two benchmark scripts: one simulating the chat QPS/concurrency using a k6-like runner (ramping to peak and holding), and one that runs the batch job at concurrency X to measure throughput and GPU utilization. We'll gather p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, and tokens/sec and cost estimates.
[02:51] Priya Nair: Can Redwood run benchmarks in a dedicated pool or do we need to provide infra?
[02:56] Marco Ruiz: For the POC we can do either: we can spin up a short-lived dedicated pool in Redwood Dedicated for controlled tests, or run in hosted with pinned instances. For highest fidelity to Nova's production, we recommend Redwood Dedicated or a private deployment clone. But for initial runs hosted is fine.
[03:12] Evan Chen: Security: we'll need SOC2 docs and KMS integration details. Also SSO/SCIM for the team.
[03:19] Aisha Patel: We'll attach our SOC2 and ISO summaries and a KMS/HSM integration guide in the POC packet. SSO SAML and SCIM provisioning are supported; we'll include setup steps.
[03:28] Sam Ortega: For traffic modeling, do you need request traces? We can export anonymized logs for a 7-day window.
[03:34] Marco Ruiz: Yes please — request traces with timestamps, payload size, and upstream routing info will help us build an accurate QPS/concurrency model. If you can't share raw content, stripped metadata with token counts per request is sufficient.
[03:45] Priya Nair: We'll provide anonymized traces and a few sample payloads. Expect that by end of next week.
[03:51] Aisha Patel: Timeline idea: week 0 (this week) finalize POC scope; week 1 run baseline benchmarks with sample inputs; week 2 tune batching/quantization and run extended tests; week 3 run final verification and deliver report. Does that align?
[04:05] Evan Chen: That aligns. We'd like a 4-week window to allow for scheduling conflicts and a security review in parallel.
[04:11] Marco Ruiz: For success criteria, propose: 1) interactive chat p95 latency under 300ms on production-like config OR a clear config that meets it (e.g., dedicated pool + model variant), 2) batch throughput hitting target tokens/hour with cost per 1M tokens under $150 using quantization options, 3) observability: Redwood Console tracing and per-route latency/cost dashboards available.
[04:31] Priya Nair: That looks good. Also add data handling requirement: no logs retained beyond 30 days for POC and support for data redaction.
[04:39] Aisha Patel: Noted — we'll include short-term retention and redaction options in the security sheet.
[04:45] Kai Thompson: One operational note: during benchmark runs we recommend warming KV caches with prefix replay to simulate real chat sessions; otherwise cold-starts skew latency.
[04:54] Marco Ruiz: Agreed — our harness will include a cache-warm step that replays typical session prefixes. We'll document how long to warm and sample size.
[05:03] Sam Ortega: About metrics: can we get token-level cost breakdown and per-route p95 in the report?
[05:09] Aisha Patel: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and per-route dashboards — we'll export a custom report after the run.
[05:15] Evan Chen: Any notes on model selection? We're currently evaluating open models and want to compare a few that are cost-effective.
[05:21] Marco Ruiz: We'll recommend a short list: a lower-latency 7B variant for chat and a higher-capacity 13B quantized variant for batch. We'll include model recommendations and perf profiles.
[05:30] Priya Nair: Great. For acceptance, after you deliver results, we'll run a short internal validation against our sample traffic and then sign off.
[05:38] Aisha Patel: To recap next steps: Redwood will send the POC packet (proposal, SOC2, benchmark harness) and schedule the benchmark window; Nova will provide traces and sample payloads and confirm test window. We aim to kick off benchmarks in the week of 2026-03-23.
[05:53] Evan Chen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[05:56] Aisha Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up by email with the artifacts.
[05:59] (call ends)
notes: Transcript contains minor transcription artifacts and occasional mis-attributions; technical details verified by SE in follow-up email.
